name: Ksamil Village Center and Beaches
description: The heart of the action, where the village clusters just back from the famous white-pebble beaches and the little offshore islets you can swim or paddle to. Restaurants, guesthouses, and beach bars line the seafront, buzzing in summer and quiet off-season.
bestFor: Beach-first slow travelers wanting to walk to the sand
pros: Steps from the best beaches and islets
Walkable to cafes, shops, and tavernas
cons: Crowded and pricey in peak summer

name: Toward Butrint National Park
description: The road south from the village toward Butrint offers a calmer, more spread-out base among olive groves, lagoon views, and scattered guesthouses. You trade beachfront immediacy for peace and proximity to the ancient ruins, wetlands, and wildlife of the national park.
bestFor: Those wanting quiet, nature, and history over nightlife
pros: Minutes from Butrint's ruins and lagoon
cons: Need transport for services and busier beaches

name: Saranda
tagline: The larger town with real services
description: A proper coastal town fifteen minutes north, Saranda is where you find banks, larger supermarkets, more reliable cafe wifi, a lively promenade, and the ferry port for Corfu. Many nomads base here for infrastructure while enjoying Ksamil's beaches on day trips.
bestFor: Nomads needing dependable services and connectivity
pros: Ferry link to Corfu for visa runs

name: Himara
tagline: Laid-back Riviera village up the coast
description: Further north along the scenic Riviera road, Himara is a relaxed coastal town with lovely beaches, a slower pace, and a more local, less overbuilt feel than Ksamil. It suits travelers wanting Riviera beauty with a calmer, more authentic atmosphere.
bestFor: Slow travelers seeking a quieter Riviera base
cons: Further from Ksamil and Saranda services
